stages.label: Define
stages.definition: A job map stage in which the job executor works to determine objectives and plan the approach.

stages.label: Locate
stages.definition: A job map stage in which the job executor works to gather the inputs and information needed.

stages.label: Prepare
stages.definition: A job map stage in which the job executor works to set up the environment and inputs.

stages.label: Confirm
stages.definition: A job map stage in which the job executor works to verify readiness before acting.

stages.label: Execute
stages.definition: A job map stage in which the job executor works to carry out the core task.

stages.label: Monitor
stages.definition: A job map stage in which the job executor works to check that the task is going as intended.

stages.label: Modify
stages.definition: A job map stage in which the job executor works to make adjustments and corrections.

stages.label: Conclude
stages.definition: A job map stage in which the job executor works to finish, close out and prepare for next time.

personas.label: Business Owner / Chief Executive Officer
personas.definition: A client persona who owns or runs a small or mid-sized client company and makes the final decision on its human resources provider and cost.
personas.context: Runs a 5–150 employee company; often the final HR decision-maker; HR is a distraction from growing the business.
personas.buying: Economic buyer — signs the agreement and owns the cost/value decision
personas.goal: Grow the business without becoming an expert in employment law, insurance and payroll tax.
emotional: Feel confident the company is not exposed to a lawsuit or penalty it doesn't know about
Feel able to compete with larger employers for talent
Be seen by employees as an employer that takes care of its people

personas.label: Finance Leader
personas.definition: A client persona who funds payroll, pays employer taxes and keeps the books, and judges the provider on total cost and accuracy.
personas.context: Owns payroll funding, tax deposits, GL posting and the HR provider invoice; frequently also the payroll processor in smaller firms.
personas.buying: Evaluator and gatekeeper on total cost; often the day-to-day payroll user
personas.goal: Keep employer costs predictable and the books accurate with minimal manual reconciliation.
emotional: Avoid the embarrassment of a missed or wrong payroll
Feel in control of every dollar of employer cost
Be seen by the owner as a trusted steward of company money
personas.titles: CFO, Controller, Office / Finance Manager who runs payroll

personas.label: Human Resources Leader
personas.definition: A client persona who runs human resources operations across every discipline, often as a team of one, and uses the provider every day.
personas.context: Covers every HR discipline at once — benefits, compliance, hiring, employee relations — with little specialist support.
personas.buying: Primary evaluator and daily user; champions or blocks the provider
personas.goal: Run reliable HR operations and spend more time on people strategy than on paperwork.
emotional: Feel confident in giving advice on issues outside their expertise
Avoid being blamed for a compliance miss
Be seen as a strategic partner rather than an administrator
personas.titles: HR Manager, HR Generalist, People Operations lead (often a team of one)

personas.label: Operations and Safety Leader
personas.definition: A client persona who is responsible for worksites where injury risk and workers' compensation cost matter to the business.
personas.context: Responsible for field or industrial worksites (construction, manufacturing, logistics, trades) where injury risk and workers' comp cost are material.
personas.buying: Influencer on risk and safety services; user of injury and safety workflows
personas.goal: Keep crews safe and productive and keep insurance cost under control.
emotional: Feel that no one will be seriously hurt on their watch
Be seen by crews as someone who has their back after an injury
personas.titles: Operations Manager, Safety Manager, Site Superintendent

personas.label: People Manager
personas.definition: A client persona who supervises a team and handles its hiring, time approval, coaching and performance conversations.
personas.context: Approves time, hires, coaches and evaluates a team; usually promoted for technical skill with little leadership training.
personas.buying: User and influencer; their experience drives employee adoption
personas.goal: Build a capable, engaged team and handle people issues well.
emotional: Feel competent handling difficult people conversations
Be seen by their team as fair and supportive

personas.label: Worksite Employee
personas.definition: A client persona who works for the client company and experiences the provider through pay, benefits, self-service and answers to questions.
personas.context: Experiences the PEO through pay, benefits, self-service and HR answers; never chose the provider.
personas.buying: End user; satisfaction affects client retention and renewal
personas.goal: Get paid correctly, understand and use benefits, and get HR tasks done without friction.
emotional: Feel financially secure and protected by good benefits
Feel respected and that personal data is handled with care
personas.titles: Any employee of the client company

personas.label: Information Technology and Systems Administrator
personas.definition: A client persona who connects employee data to other business systems and is accountable for its access and security.
personas.context: Connects HR and payroll data to accounting, scheduling and identity systems; responsible for access and security.
personas.buying: Technical evaluator; can veto on security or integration grounds
personas.goal: Keep employee data flowing between systems accurately and securely with little maintenance.
emotional: Avoid being responsible for a data breach involving employee records
personas.titles: IT Manager, Systems Administrator, outsourced MSP

proposals.label: Employee Expense Reimbursement Service
proposals.why: Insperity lists expense management as a product; add it to the model so it can be traced to jobs and delivered through the payroll steps it touches.

proposals.label: Outplacement & Career Transition Service
proposals.why: Insperity is the only provider in the landscape that offers outplacement. It belongs in the model, next to the separation questions it answers.

proposals.label: Business Insurance Brokerage Service
proposals.why: Insperity sells business insurance; the model has no service for it, so it cannot be bundled with risk profiling or renewals.

proposals.label: Partner Marketplace Service
proposals.why: Insperity MarketPlace exists; naming it as a service lets connectors and partner offers be governed like any other service.

proposals.label: Earned Wage Access Service
proposals.why: Paychex embedded on-demand pay in its PEO in 2026 and ADP offers it through Wisely. A partner can supply the funding; the pay rules and limits belong in the rules register.

proposals.label: Unemployment Claims Administration Service
proposals.why: ADP and Paychex list it. Each unemployment claim affects the state unemployment rate the co-employer pays.

proposals.label: Employer Tax Credit Identification & Recovery Service
proposals.why: Paychex screens every payroll client for hiring and location credits; TriNet bought an R&D credit business. Eligibility is a set of rules over hires, locations and wages that the rules register can evaluate for every client.

proposals.label: Affordable Care Act Employer Mandate & Information Reporting Service
proposals.why: TriNet names it; the model covers continuation coverage but not measurement periods, affordability tests or the annual reporting.

proposals.label: Commuter Benefits
proposals.why: Add to the tax-advantaged accounts service rather than a new service.

proposals.label: Individual Coverage Health Reimbursement Arrangement Service
proposals.why: Only Justworks offers it, through a partner, launched in 2026. Watch take-up; it competes with the master health plan.

proposals.label: Mental Health & Family-Forming Benefits Service
proposals.why: Justworks bundles these in its top tier; they answer the candidate and retention questions on benefits.

proposals.label: Pooled Employer Plan Option
proposals.why: Paychex offers a pooled employer plan. Compare fiduciary allocation and cost against the existing multiple employer plan before changing anything.

proposals.label: Cyber Liability Insurance Service
proposals.why: Paychex lists cyber liability in its Oasis offer. A partner product, priced from the client risk profile (R01).

proposals.label: Dedicated HR Business Partner Service
proposals.why: Every provider names the advisor relationship; in the model it is only implied by escalation and retention. Making it a service lets its outcomes be measured.

proposals.label: Employee Relations Advisory & Investigation Service
proposals.why: Competitors advise before a claim; the model only defends after one.

proposals.label: Industry Practice Advisory Service
proposals.why: TriNet sells seven industry teams. Industry rule sets and process variants can be modeled once and reused, so an industry practice is a configuration, not a separate team.

insperity.n: No packaged verticals in public material

proposals.label: Applicant Tracking & Job Distribution Service
proposals.why: Most competitors sell applicant tracking on its own; the model has it only inside recruiting outsourcing.

proposals.label: Headcount & Workforce Planning Service
proposals.why: Rippling sells headcount planning. Workforce plans join headcount, cost and budget, which the knowledge layer already relates.

proposals.label: Device & Application Management Service
proposals.why: Only Rippling offers it and it sits outside the PEO’s role. Answer the first-day access and offboarding questions through identity integration and the partner marketplace instead.

proposals.label: International Employer of Record Service
proposals.why: Four of the six competitors offer it. A partner network can carry the local employment; the knowledge layer holds each country’s rules.

proposals.label: International Contractor Management & Payments Service
proposals.why: Justworks pays contractors in 50+ countries and converts them to employees through its EOR.

proposals.label: Regulatory Change Intelligence Service
proposals.why: Matches the client’s footprint (states, cities, headcount thresholds, industry) against the versioned rules register and tells the client which obligations changed, when they take effect and which of their process steps they govern. Rippling’s Compliance 360 flags violations; this explains the obligation and its source.

proposals.label: Obligation-to-Control Mapping & Audit Evidence Service
proposals.why: Each obligation is linked to the process steps it governs, the control that meets it and the record that proves it, so an agency or auditor request becomes a query that returns an evidence pack with its provenance.

proposals.label: Pre-Payroll Rule Validation Service
proposals.why: Every pay run is checked against minimum wage, overtime, break, final-pay and accrual rules for each employee’s jurisdiction before funds are released. ADP’s payroll agent audits variances; this checks against the rules themselves and cites them.

proposals.label: Worker Classification Decision Service
proposals.why: Exempt and contractor tests differ by state. A decision model asks the decision questions, applies the rules and records the rationale.

proposals.label: Automated Employment Decision Compliance Service
proposals.why: Clients that use AI in hiring, pay or performance decisions now owe notices, adverse-action steps and records (Illinois from 2026, Colorado from 2027). The service inventories the client’s decision tools, issues the notices, measures disparate impact and keeps the records.

proposals.label: Pay Equity & Pay Transparency Compliance Service
proposals.why: Pay transparency rules vary by state and city; pay gaps need job-related explanations. The rules register and the job architecture make both checkable.

proposals.label: Client Employer Risk Profile Service
proposals.why: One profile per client, built from compliance posture, workers’ compensation class and claims, employment practices signals, turnover, tax history and benefits experience. Underwriting, pricing and the advisor use the same explained profile, and the client sees risks before they become costs.

proposals.label: Workers’ Compensation Class & Claims Risk Analytics Service
proposals.why: Checks each employee’s class code against duties and predicts injury risk by worksite, feeding the safety survey.

proposals.label: Employment Practices Exposure Early Warning Service
proposals.why: Watches terminations, complaints, documentation gaps and rating patterns for exposure, within the privacy safeguards, and alerts the advisor.

proposals.label: Benefits Cost & Renewal Risk Forecast Service
proposals.why: Forecasts the client’s renewal from plan mix, demographics and claims trend, months before renewal.

proposals.label: Governed Decision Support Service
proposals.why: Decision models for recurring decisions (leave eligibility, discipline, offers, pay changes): the decision questions to answer, the rules that apply, a recommended course and the rationale recorded for later review.

proposals.label: Benefits Plan Design Optimizer Service
proposals.why: Optimizes plan mix and contributions against budget, employee preferences and peer benchmarks; the same model helps employees choose a plan.

proposals.label: Total Cost of Employment Scenario Service
proposals.why: Publishes the internal total cost of employment model to clients: the fully loaded cost of an employee, of a workforce change and of the PEO itself. It answers the price-transparency questions Justworks answers with a price list.

proposals.label: Workforce Benchmark Data Product
proposals.why: Peer benchmarks for pay, turnover, benefits and safety across the client base, de-identified and aggregated under the existing thresholds.

proposals.label: Client Workforce Knowledge Graph Service
proposals.why: A governed semantic layer over the client’s HR data and the business systems it connects to, so ad hoc questions get consistent answers and field mappings are validated, not guessed.

proposals.label: Grounded HR Policy & Pay Answer Agent Service
proposals.why: Answers employee and manager questions from the client’s own handbook, the jurisdiction’s rules and the employee’s pay data, citing the rule and version behind each answer. ADP launched an HR policy agent in 2026; the difference is grounding and measured accuracy.

insperity.n: AI initiatives cited on Q2 2026 call

proposals.label: Agent Accuracy Measurement & Calibration Service
proposals.why: Metrology for agents: reference question sets drawn from the 250 customer questions, measured accuracy, groundedness and citation validity with uncertainty, drift tracking, and a measurement record for every agent release. It is what lets a client or a regulator trust an agent’s answer.

proposals.label: Agent Guardrail & Circuit-Breaker Service
proposals.why: Every agent action passes the validation gate (shapes, then rules, then policy). When measured error rates cross a threshold the circuit breaker stops the agent and routes the work to a person.

proposals.label: Decision Provenance & Explainability Ledger Service
proposals.why: A provenance record for every agent action and decision: inputs, rules and versions, model, reviewer and outcome. It meets the record-keeping duties of the new automated decision laws and lets a decision be explained or reversed.

proposals.label: Client AI and Agent Governance Service
proposals.why: Helps clients inventory and govern their own AI tools that touch employee data: purpose, risk tier, notices, monitoring and measured performance, using the same gateway the PEO uses on itself.

ssot.label: Rules, constraints and logic (SSOT)
ssot.description: The governed register of rules, constraints and calculations, versioned, with impact analysis (SSOT Rules Map, SSOT Editor).

dq.label: Decision question baseline
dq.description: The decision and competency questions each decision must answer, with its obligations, permissions and prohibitions.

ontology.label: Core domain ontology
ontology.description: The unifying ontology anchored on the process step: who performs it, what it consumes and produces, which rules govern it and which measures evaluate it (BFO-aligned).

shacl.label: Shapes and conformance
shacl.description: SHACL shapes and Part III conformance checks that validate data and assertions before they are used.

gateway.label: Semantic gateway
gateway.description: The requirements engineering semantic gateway: traced, reviewed, evidenced, measurable, owned and unflagged before admission.

agents.label: Governed agents
agents.description: Agents behind a validation gate (SHACL, then rules, then policy enforcement), with circuit breakers, human review and recorded commits.

prov.label: Provenance and versioning
prov.description: PROV-O change records, semantic versioning and named graphs for every asset and decision.

c360.label: Customer 360
c360.description: Personas, jobs to be done, desired outcomes and their measured importance and satisfaction.

privacy.label: Privacy-preserving analytics
privacy.description: Purpose limitation, notice and consent, de-identification and aggregation thresholds, retention (the Privacy-Preserving People Analytics context).

measures.label: Measures and metrology
measures.description: Measures attached to process steps (SIPOCM), with definitions, units, targets and measured values that can be traced and calibrated.

apqc.label: Process registry and assemblies
apqc.description: APQC-anchored processes and the service assemblies that show which internal steps deliver each service.

paychex-pep.title: Paychex introduces a pooled employer 401(k) plan (Paychex)

colorado-ai.title: Colorado S.B. 26-189 replaces the Colorado AI Act; notice, adverse-action and record duties from 2027-01-01 (Littler)
